definition_en: in or to a higher place than something, or more than a number
core_image: 一盏灯挂得比桌面更高，光从上面落下来
scene: 厨房的灯挂得高过桌面，光从上面铺下来。The lamp hangs above the kitchen table.
sceneCN: 这里 above 是「位置更高」（第 01 个义项）；句意是灯挂在桌子上方。

derivatives.zh: 上文提到的，由 above 与 mentioned 复合
光明正大的，由 above 与 board 复合

senses.title: Higher than something in space
senses.definition: in or at a position higher than something else
senses.definitionCN: 位置高于某物
senses.example: The lamp hangs above the table.
senses.exampleCN: 灯挂在桌子上方。
senses.why: Above comes from Old English abufan, literally 'up over', so its oldest job is to mark a higher place; the lamp over the table is that literal use.
senses.whyCN: above 来自古英语 abufan，字面是「在上方」，最古老的任务就是标出更高的位置；灯挂在桌面上方正是这层本义。

senses.title: More than a stated amount
senses.definition: more than a particular number, amount or level
senses.definitionCN: 多于某个数字、数量或水平
senses.example: Temperatures rose above thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 气温升到三十度以上。
senses.why: Height can be measured and so can amounts: passing a figure puts you over it, which is why above moved from space to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 高度可以量，数目也可以量；越过某个数字就像站到了那个刻度的上方，above 因此从空间挪到数量。

senses.title: Higher in rank or importance
senses.definition: having a higher rank or greater importance than someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 等级或重要性高于某人某物
senses.example: She ranks above him in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在办公室里的级别高于他。
senses.why: A rank list is a vertical ladder in the mind, with the higher post drawn above the lower one, so above came to mean greater rank.
senses.whyCN: 职位表在头脑里像一架竖梯，高一级的位置画在低一级上方，above 于是表示等级更高。

senses.title: Earlier in a piece of writing
senses.definition: appearing earlier on the same page or in an earlier part of a text
senses.definitionCN: 出现在同一页更靠前的位置或文本的前面部分
senses.example: See the note above.
senses.exampleCN: 见上文的注释。
senses.why: A page is read from top to bottom, so whatever was read first sits physically above the present line; hence above means 'earlier in the text'.
senses.whyCN: 书页自上而下读，先读到的内容在纸面上就位于现在这一行的上方，所以 above 指「上文」。

senses.title: Too good or proud to do something
senses.definition: considering oneself too good, honest or proud to do something
senses.definitionCN: 自认为品格或身份较高而不屑做某事
senses.example: He is above such tricks.
senses.exampleCN: 他不屑于玩这种把戏。
senses.why: If you place a trick beneath you, you stand above it; the spatial picture turns into a judgement of character, giving 'too proud for'.
senses.whyCN: 把某种把戏看得低、自己站在它上方，空间画面就变成对人的评判，于是有了「不屑于」这层意思。

items.cn: 古英语 abufan，由 a- 与 bufan 构成，意为在上。

items.en: The second element relates to be- plus ufan, a Germanic word for over.
items.cn: 后一成分与 be- 加 ufan 相关，是表示「在上」的日耳曼词。

items.en: The family points to *upo, 'up from under'.
items.cn: 这一组词指向 *upo「从下往上」。

items.en: The forms merged into the single word above.
items.cn: 中古英语时期各形式合并为 above。

items.en: The word widened from place to quantity, rank and preference.
items.cn: 现代英语中从位置扩展到数量、等级与优先。

definition_en: later than something in time, or behind something in space or order
core_image: 一个人走过门槛之后，另一个人跟着踏进同一块影子
scene: 午后的教室空了，最后一个孩子把门带上才离开。We walked home after the last class.
sceneCN: 这里 after 是「时间上在后」（第 01 个义项）；句意是最后一节课结束后我们走路回家。

derivatives.zh: 之后，由 after 加 -wards 构成
下午，由 after 与 noon 复合

senses.title: Later than an event
senses.definition: later in time than something else
senses.definitionCN: 时间上晚于某事
senses.example: We walked home after the last class.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一节课结束后我们走路回家。
senses.why: After goes back to Old English æfter, 'behind, following'; when what follows is an event rather than a thing, the word marks later time.
senses.whyCN: after 源自中古英语 æfter，本义是「在后面、跟着」；当跟着的是事件而不是物体时，它就标记时间上更晚。

senses.title: Behind in place or order
senses.definition: following something in place, order or sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在位置或顺序上紧跟在某物之后
senses.example: Put a comma after the last word.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一个词后面加一个逗号。
senses.why: The same 'following' picture applies to a line of words or a queue, where the next item stands behind the previous one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「跟着」的画面也能用在字词排列或队伍上：后一项就排在前一项的后面。

senses.title: In pursuit of
senses.definition: running or moving behind someone in order to catch them
senses.definitionCN: 跟在某人后面跑，想追上他
senses.example: The dog ran after the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 狗追着球跑。
senses.why: Chasing is following made active: the pursuer stays behind the thing he wants, so the old sense of 'behind' turns into pursuit.
senses.whyCN: 追赶是「跟着」的动作版：追的人始终落在目标后面，于是「在后面」这层旧义变成了追赶。

senses.title: In honour or imitation of
senses.definition: using the name of someone, or copying the style of something
senses.definitionCN: 用某人的名字命名，或照着某物的样式做
senses.example: The street is named after her.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街以她的名字命名。
senses.why: A name given 'after' a person is one that follows that person around, and a style copied 'after' a model follows it closely; both rest on the same following image.
senses.whyCN: 以某人命名，就是让这个名字跟着他走；仿照某种样式，就是让做法紧跟着那个样板；两者都建立在「跟随」这个画面上。

definition_en: the whole of something, every member of a group, or completely
core_image: 一只大篮子把桌上的东西一件不剩地装进去
scene: 收摊的时候，摊主把剩下的东西一起装进大筐。She packed all the books into one box.
sceneCN: 这里 all 是「全部」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她把所有的书装进一个箱子。

derivatives.zh: 几乎，由 al 与 most 合成
已经，由 al 与 ready 合成
完全地，由 al 与 together 合成

senses.title: The whole of a group or amount
senses.definition: the whole number or amount of something, with no part left out
senses.definitionCN: 整体的全部，一部分也不缺
senses.example: She packed all the books into one box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把所有的书都装进一个箱子。
senses.why: All descends from Old English eall, 'whole, entire', and the picture is a basket that takes every item off the table without leaving one behind.
senses.whyCN: all 来自古英语 eall「完整的、全部的」，画面是一只篮子把桌上的东西一件不剩地装走。

senses.title: Everything
senses.definition: every thing, used as a pronoun without naming the things
senses.definitionCN: 作代词，指所有事物，不必说出具体是什么
senses.example: All was quiet in the house.
senses.exampleCN: 屋子里一切都安静。
senses.why: When the noun is already understood, English drops it and lets all stand alone, so the same wholeness becomes the pronoun 'everything'.
senses.whyCN: 当所指的事物已经不言自明，英语就把名词省掉，让 all 单独站着，同样的「整体」于是变成代词「一切」。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: entirely, used to strengthen an adjective or a phrase
senses.definitionCN: 完全地，用来加强形容词或短语
senses.example: She was all alone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自一人待在房间里。
senses.why: Wholeness applied to a quality rather than a set gives the adverb 'completely': the person is wholly, entirely alone.
senses.whyCN: 把「整体」用在性质而不是集合上，就得到副词「完全地」：她完完全全一个人。

senses.title: The only thing
senses.definition: the single thing that matters in a statement
senses.definitionCN: 一句话里唯一要紧的那件事
senses.example: All I want is a cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 我只想要一杯茶。
senses.why: If the whole field of desire is narrowed to one item, all in front of a clause means 'the only thing'.
senses.whyCN: 把整个愿望的范围收窄到一样东西，all 放在从句前就表示「唯一的东西」。

items.en: Germanic *allaz is behind German all and Dutch al.

items.cn: 现代英语中 all 覆盖群体、整体、时段与强调。

definition_en: in addition, or in the same way
core_image: 一只手把第二样东西也放进已经装满的口袋
scene: 清单写到一半，主人想起还有一样东西没记上。She sings and also writes her own songs.
sceneCN: 这里 also 是「也」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她唱歌，也自己写歌。

derivatives.zh: 落选者，由 also 与 ran 复合
落选者们的复数，由 also-ran 加 -s 构成

senses.title: In addition
senses.definition: in addition to something already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在已提到的事物之外再加一个
senses.example: She sings and also writes her own songs.
senses.exampleCN: 她唱歌，也自己写歌。
senses.why: Also is a compressed form of Old English ealswā, 'all so, quite so'; if a second thing is 'quite so' as the first, it is simply added, giving 'too'.
senses.whyCN: also 是古英语 ealswā「完全如此」的缩合形式；第二件事和第一件「完全一样」，就是简单地追加，于是表示「也」。

senses.title: At the start of a sentence, adding a further point
senses.definition: used at the beginning of a sentence to add a further point or reason
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，补充另一条信息或理由
senses.example: Also, bring a pencil to the test.
senses.exampleCN: 另外，考试要带一支铅笔。
senses.why: At the front of a sentence the word no longer modifies one phrase; it links the whole sentence to what came before, so it becomes the connective 'besides'.
senses.whyCN: 放到句首后，这个词不再只修饰一个短语，而是把整句接到上文之后，于是变成连接性的「此外」。

items.cn: 古英语 ealswā 由 eall「全部」与 swā「如此」合成。

items.en: It first meant 'wholly so', then 'likewise'.
items.cn: 最初意为「完全如此」，后转为「同样」。

items.en: The form contracted to also, with the same adding sense.
items.cn: 中古英语时期缩略为 also，保留添加义。

items.en: Also became the standard written word for addition.
items.cn: 现代英语中 also 成为书面语里表示添加的标准词。

items.en: In speech, too and as well often replace it.
items.cn: 口语中常用 too 与 as well 替代。

definition_en: at all times, every time, or forever
core_image: 钟摆一秒也不停，始终在同一个弧线上来回
scene: 院里的老钟走了很多年，指针从来没被调过。The old clock always shows the right time.
sceneCN: 这里 always 是「总是」（第 01 个义项）；句意是那座老钟的时间总是准的。

derivatives.zh: always 的古旧形式
常开的，由 always 与 on 复合

senses.title: Every time, without exception
senses.definition: on every occasion, with no exception
senses.definitionCN: 每一次都如此，没有例外
senses.example: The old clock always shows the right time.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老钟的时间总是准的。
senses.why: Always comes from Old English ealne weg, 'the whole way', and a journey that lasts the whole way never stops, so the word means 'on every occasion'.
senses.whyCN: always 来自古英语 ealne weg「整条路」；走完整条路从未停下，所以这个词表示「每一次都」。

senses.title: For ever
senses.definition: for all future time, without end
senses.definitionCN: 在未来所有时间里，没有尽头
senses.example: I will always remember her kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 我会永远记得她的好意。
senses.why: Stretch that whole-way picture past the present into all coming time and the same word means 'for ever'.
senses.whyCN: 把「整条路」的画面从现在拉向所有未来的时间，同一个词就表示「永远」。

senses.title: Repeatedly, as a habit
senses.definition: again and again, often said with annoyance about a habit
senses.definitionCN: 一再发生，常带抱怨地指某种习惯
senses.example: He is always losing his keys.
senses.exampleCN: 他老是把钥匙弄丢。
senses.why: With a progressive verb the focus shifts from every single occasion to the endless repetition itself, which is why it sounds like a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 和进行时连用时，重点从「每一次」转到「没完没了地重复」，所以听起来像抱怨。

definition_en: relating to the United States or to the Americas, or a person from them
core_image: 一面星条旗在风里展开，旗杆下站着来自各地的人
scene: 街角的咖啡馆里，墙上挂着一张旧地图，标着另一块大陆。She married an American and moved to Chicago.
sceneCN: 这里 american 是「美国人」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她嫁给了一个美国人，搬去了芝加哥。

senses.title: A person from the United States
senses.definition: a citizen or inhabitant of the United States
senses.definitionCN: 美国的公民或居民
senses.example: She married an American and moved to Chicago.
senses.exampleCN: 她嫁给了一个美国人，搬去了芝加哥。
senses.why: American adds -an to America, a name taken from the explorer Amerigo Vespucci; the noun use names a person who belongs to that country.
senses.whyCN: American 是 America 加 -an。America 取自航海家亚美利哥·韦斯普奇的名字；名词用法指属于这个国家的人。

senses.title: Relating to the United States
senses.definition: of or belonging to the United States, its people or its culture
senses.definitionCN: 属于美国、美国人或美国文化的
senses.example: American English differs from British English.
senses.exampleCN: 美式英语和英式英语不同。
senses.why: The same -an ending also makes an adjective, so the word can describe anything that belongs to the United States.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -an 词尾也构成形容词，于是这个词能描述任何属于美国的事物。

senses.title: Relating to the Americas
senses.definition: of or belonging to North or South America as continents
senses.definitionCN: 属于北美洲或南美洲这片大陆的
senses.example: Spanish is spoken across much of the American continent.
senses.exampleCN: 美洲大陆的大部分地区都讲西班牙语。
senses.why: Before the United States existed, America named the whole western continent, and that older geographic sense survives in the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 美国建国之前，America 指整个美洲大陆，这个更早的地理义至今仍保留在形容词用法里。

items.en: The name America comes from the explorer Amerigo Vespucci.
items.cn: America 之名来自航海家亚美利哥·韦斯普奇。

items.en: The Latinised form Americus named the new lands on maps.
items.cn: 拉丁化形式 Americus 在地图上命名新大陆。

items.en: American entered English in the sixteenth century for the Americas.
items.cn: American 在十六世纪进入英语，指美洲。

items.en: After independence the word increasingly meant the United States.
items.cn: 独立之后，这个词越来越多地指美国。

items.en: American now covers the continents, the country and its people.
items.cn: 现代用法中 American 覆盖大陆、国家与国民。

definition_en: a living creature that is not a plant, especially one with a body and senses
core_image: 草地上一只四足的生物低头吃草，耳朵随时警觉
scene: 天快黑时，林边的草地上还有几只生物低着头。The farmer fed the animals before dark.
sceneCN: 这里 animal 是「动物」（第 01 个义项）；句意是天黑前农夫喂了牲口。

senses.title: A living creature that is not a plant
senses.definition: a living thing that is not a plant, usually able to move and sense
senses.definitionCN: 有生命、通常能移动和感知的非植物生物
senses.example: The farmer fed the animals before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天快黑时，农夫喂了牲口。
senses.why: Animal comes from Latin animalis, 'having breath', from anima, 'breath, life'; anything that breathes and senses is an animal, as opposed to a plant.
senses.whyCN: animal 来自拉丁语 animalis「有气息的」，源于 anima「气息、生命」；凡是会呼吸、有感知的生物就是 animal，与植物相对。

senses.title: A creature other than a human
senses.definition: a creature other than a human being
senses.definitionCN: 人以外的生物
senses.example: The zoo keeps animals from many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 动物园养着来自许多国家的动物。
senses.why: Because people usually speak about themselves separately, the everyday word narrowed to the creatures around us, the ones a zoo keeps.
senses.whyCN: 因为人习惯把自己单独拿出来说，这个词在日常里就收窄为人类以外的生灵，也就是动物园里养的那些。

senses.title: A brutal person
senses.definition: a person who behaves in a wild, cruel or unfeeling way
senses.definitionCN: 行为野蛮、残忍或没有同情心的人
senses.example: He behaved like an animal at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上表现得像个野兽。
senses.why: Calling a person an animal borrows the wildness of a beast to judge his behaviour, so the word becomes an insult.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作 animal，是借野兽的野性来评判他的行为，这个词因此成了骂人的说法。

senses.title: Relating to animals
senses.definition: of or for animals, used before another noun
senses.definitionCN: 动物的，放在另一名词前作定语
senses.example: The coat is lined with animal fur.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套用动物毛皮做衬里。
senses.why: English often puts a noun before another noun like an adjective, so animal in animal fur simply means 'of animals'.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把名词放在另一名词前当形容词用，所以 animal fur 里的 animal 就是「动物的」。

definition_en: one or some, no matter which, used in questions, negatives and general statements
core_image: 一只空盘子举起来，问谁都可以往里放一样东西
scene: 桌上只剩一只空盘，主人问了一圈谁还要添点东西。Is there any water left in the jug?
sceneCN: 这里 any 是疑问句里的「一些」（第 01 个义项）；句意是壶里还剩水吗。

derivatives.zh: 任何人，由 any 与 one 复合
任何事物，由 any 与 thing 复合
任何地方，由 any 与 where 复合

senses.title: Some or one, in questions and negatives
senses.titleCN: 一些；任何一个（疑问、否定）
senses.definition: one or some, used when it is not known whether the thing exists
senses.definitionCN: 不确定是否存在时，指一个或一些
senses.example: Is there any water left in the jug?
senses.exampleCN: 壶里还剩水吗？
senses.why: Any began as Old English ǣnig, 'one', from ān plus a suffix; when the speaker does not know whether even one exists, that 'one' turns into a question word for amount.
senses.whyCN: any 最初是古英语 ǣnig「一个」，由 ān 加词尾构成；说话人连「有没有一个」都不确定时，这个「一个」就变成疑问和否定里的量词。

senses.title: No matter which, every
senses.definition: every one, whichever is chosen, with no exception
senses.definitionCN: 随便哪一个都，无一例外
senses.example: Any child can join the club.
senses.exampleCN: 任何孩子都能加入这个社团。
senses.why: Push 'one, whichever it is' to its limit and every member qualifies, so any means 'no matter which'.
senses.whyCN: 把「随便哪一个」推到极限，每个成员都符合，any 就表示「无论哪个」。

senses.title: At all, with a comparative
senses.definition: in the least, used before a comparative to strengthen it
senses.definitionCN: 一点也不，放在比较级前加强语气
senses.example: He isn't any better today.
senses.exampleCN: 他今天一点也没好转。
senses.why: Before a comparative the word stops counting things and only adds force, like saying 'not even a little'.
senses.whyCN: 放在比较级前时，这个词不再数东西，只加语气，相当于说「一点也不」。

definition_en: the fourth month of the year, between March and May
core_image: 雨里刚冒出的新芽，叶子还没完全展开
scene: 连着下了几天雨，院角的土里冒出细细的绿芽。The garden wakes up in April after the long rain.
sceneCN: 这里 april 是「四月」（第 01 个义项）；句意是漫长雨季过后，园子在四月苏醒。

derivatives.zh: 愚人节玩笑，由 April 与 fool 复合

senses.title: The fourth month of the year
senses.definition: the fourth month of the year, between March and May
senses.definitionCN: 一年中的第四个月，在三月和五月之间
senses.example: The garden wakes up in April after the long rain.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长雨季过后，园子在四月苏醒。
senses.why: April comes from Latin Aprilis, the month that opened the Roman spring; it kept that place at the head of spring when the calendar moved.
senses.whyCN: April 来自拉丁语 Aprilis，是罗马春天开始的那个月；历法调整后，它仍守着春季开端的那个位置。

senses.title: A female given name
senses.definition: a girl's name taken from the name of the month
senses.definitionCN: 由月份名转来的女子名
senses.example: April is my cousin's name.
senses.exampleCN: 阿普丽尔是我表姐的名字。
senses.why: Because the month stands at the opening of spring, the month name has also long served as a girl's name in English, written with a capital A.
senses.whyCN: 四月正当春天的开端，这个月份名在英语里也长期用作女孩的名字，书写时首字母大写。

items.en: April was the second month of the old Roman year.

definition_zh: 姑母；姨母；舅母；伯母；阿姨
definition_en: the sister of one's father or mother, or the wife of one's uncle
core_image: 一位年长的女性坐在桌边，把糖果分给围过来的孩子
scene: 过年的时候，那位总带着糖果来的长辈坐在炕边。My aunt brought a box of sweets for the children.
sceneCN: 这里 aunt 是「姑母或姨母」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我姑姑住在河对岸。

pos.zh: 名词：姑母、姨母、舅母、伯母

derivatives.zh: 由 aunt 加 -ie 构成的亲昵称呼
由 aunt 加 -y 构成的亲昵称呼
由 great 与 aunt 复合，义为「曾祖辈的姑姨」

senses.title: The sister of your father or mother
senses.definition: the sister of one's father or mother
senses.definitionCN: 父亲或母亲的姐妹
senses.example: My aunt lives across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我姑姑住在河对岸。
senses.why: Aunt came into English from Old French ante, from Latin amita, 'father's sister'; English widened it so the mother's sister is also aunt.
senses.whyCN: aunt 从古法语 ante 进入英语，源头是拉丁语 amita「父亲的姐妹」；英语把范围扩大，母亲的姐妹也叫 aunt。

senses.title: The wife of your uncle
senses.definition: the wife of one's uncle
senses.definitionCN: 叔伯或舅舅的妻子
senses.example: Aunt Mary is my uncle's wife.
senses.exampleCN: 玛丽婶婶是我叔叔的妻子。
senses.why: A woman who joins the family by marrying an uncle takes the same title, because the word names a role in the household, not only a blood link.
senses.whyCN: 通过嫁给叔伯舅舅而进入家庭的女性也用同一个称呼，因为这个词标的是家庭里的位置，而不只是血缘。

senses.title: An unrelated older woman close to the family
senses.definition: an unrelated older woman addressed affectionately by a child
senses.definitionCN: 孩子亲昵称呼的、没有血缘关系的年长女性
senses.example: Aunt Li often brings sweets to the children.
senses.exampleCN: 李阿姨常给孩子们带糖。
senses.why: Children extend the family word to friendly older women, so aunt can be a warm form of address with no kinship at all.
senses.whyCN: 孩子把这个家庭称谓扩展到亲近的年长女性，于是 aunt 可以完全没有血缘，只是一种亲切的称呼。

items.cn: 拉丁语 amita 指父亲的姐妹。

items.en: Old French ante carried the family word into English.
items.cn: 古法语 ante 把这个亲属词带入英语。

items.en: Middle English aunte settled as aunt.
items.cn: 中古英语 aunte 固定为 aunt。

items.en: Some older sources link the word to a child's form of 'mother'.
items.cn: 一些较早文献把它与儿语的「母亲」形式联系起来。

items.cn: 现代英语中 aunt 覆盖父母的姐妹、叔伯的妻子与亲切称呼。

definition_en: the season between summer and winter, when leaves fall
core_image: 树叶由绿转黄，一片片落在地上铺成一层
scene: 风一过，院里的叶子落了一地，扫帚刚扫过又铺上。The leaves turn gold in autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 autumn 是「秋季」（第 01 个义项）；句意是秋天叶子变成金黄色。

derivatives.zh: 由 autumn 加 -al 构成，义为「秋季的」
由 autumnal 加 -ly 构成，义为「如秋地」

senses.title: The season between summer and winter
senses.definition: the season between summer and winter, when leaves fall
senses.definitionCN: 夏季与冬季之间、树叶凋落的季节
senses.example: The leaves turn gold in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天叶子变成金黄色。
senses.why: Autumn comes from Latin autumnus, the Roman name for the season of harvest and falling leaves, and English kept that place in the year.
senses.whyCN: autumn 来自拉丁语 autumnus，是罗马人对收获与落叶季节的称呼，英语保留了它在一年中的位置。

senses.title: The later, maturing part of life
senses.definition: the later stage of a life or of a period, seen as its mature part
senses.definitionCN: 人生或某个时期走向成熟的后半段
senses.example: He saw the autumn of his life approaching.
senses.exampleCN: 他看见自己人生的秋季正在临近。
senses.why: Harvest comes and leaves fall after the full summer, and a life that has passed its prime looks the same, so autumn can name its later stage.
senses.whyCN: 盛夏过后收获来临、叶子落下，人生过了鼎盛也像这样，于是 autumn 可以指它的后半段。

intro.en: The history of autumn is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: autumn 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Autumnus was the Latin name of the season.
items.cn: Autumnus 是这个季节的拉丁名称。

items.en: The Latin word's own origin is uncertain; it may be Etruscan.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词本身的来源不确定，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语。

items.en: Old French automne carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 古法语 automne 把它带向英语。

items.en: English borrowed autumn in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 autumn。

items.en: American English prefers fall, a native word for the season.
items.cn: 美式英语更常用本族词 fall 指这个季节。

definition_en: a game in which players throw a ball through a high hoop, or the ball used
core_image: 一只橙色的球被抛向高处的圆环，网绳轻轻一颤
scene: 操场的篮架下，几个孩子把球传来传去，等着出手。They played basketball until the light faded.
sceneCN: 这里 basketball 是「篮球运动」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们打篮球打到天光暗下去。

derivatives.zh: 由 basketball 加 -er 构成，义为「篮球运动员」（口语）
由 basketball 与 court 复合，义为「篮球场」

senses.title: The game played with a ball and a high basket
senses.definition: a game in which two teams try to throw a ball through a high net
senses.definitionCN: 两队把球投进高处的篮网的运动
senses.example: They played basketball until the light faded.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打篮球一直打到天光暗下去。
senses.why: The name joins basket and ball, and the game is named after its two fixed pieces: the ball and the basket it must reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字由 basket 和 ball 合成，这项运动正是以它固定的两样东西命名：球，以及球要投进的篮筐。

senses.title: The ball used in that game
senses.definition: the large round ball used in the game of basketball
senses.definitionCN: 篮球运动中使用的大圆球
senses.example: He bounced the basketball twice before shooting.
senses.exampleCN: 他投篮前把篮球拍了两下。
senses.why: Taken word by word, basketball is simply 'basket ball', the ball aimed at the basket, and that literal object is still the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 逐字看，basketball 就是「篮子球」，即投向篮筐的那颗球；这个字面所指的实物仍是它的第二个义项。

items.cn: basketball 由 basket 与 ball 组合，十九世纪九十年代造出。

items.en: The game was invented by James Naismith in 1891.
items.cn: 这项运动由詹姆斯·奈史密斯于 1891 年发明。

items.en: Early players used peach baskets as goals.
items.cn: 早期球员用装桃子的篮子当球筐。

items.en: The compound names the game, the ball and the court.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个复合词指运动、球与场地。

items.en: The word spread with the sport around the world.
items.cn: 这个词随运动传遍世界。

definition_en: a room with a bath or shower, or a room with a toilet
core_image: 一间小屋里瓷砖泛着水光，毛巾挂在门后
scene: 楼道的尽头有一扇窄门，门后是家里唯一有镜子的地方。She went to the bathroom to wash her hands.
sceneCN: 这里 bathroom 是「浴室」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她去洗手间洗手。

derivatives.zh: 由本词前一成分独立成词，义为「洗澡、浴缸」
带浴室的，由 bathroom 加 -ed 构成

senses.title: A room with a bath or shower
senses.definition: a room in a house containing a bath or shower
senses.definitionCN: 住宅里装有浴缸或淋浴设备的房间
senses.example: The bathroom has a new shower.
senses.exampleCN: 浴室里装了新的淋浴。
senses.why: Bathroom is simply bath plus room, so its first meaning is the room where the bath is taken.
senses.whyCN: bathroom 就是 bath 加 room，字面即「洗澡的房间」，所以它最基本的意思是供人洗澡的屋子。

senses.title: A room with a toilet, in American use
senses.definition: a room containing a toilet, the usual American word for it
senses.definitionCN: 装有马桶的房间，美式英语常用的委婉说法
senses.example: She went to the bathroom to wash her hands.
senses.exampleCN: 她去洗手间洗手。
senses.why: American speakers avoid naming the toilet directly and use bathroom for the whole room instead, so the word added this polite sense.
senses.whyCN: 美国人说话不愿直接提马桶，就用 bathroom 代指整个房间，这个词因此多了一层委婉的「洗手间」义。

intro.en: The history of bathroom is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bathroom 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Bathroom joins bath and room, recorded from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: bathroom 由 bath 与 room 复合，十八世纪已有记录。

items.en: Bath comes from Old English bæþ, a place for washing.
items.cn: bath 来自古英语 bæþ，指洗浴之处。

items.en: Room comes from Old English rūm, meaning space.
items.cn: room 来自古英语 rūm，意为空间。

items.en: In American English bathroom came to mean a toilet room.
items.cn: 在美式英语中 bathroom 转而指带厕所的房间。

items.en: The word covers private, public and hotel washing spaces.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词覆盖私人、公共与旅馆的洗浴空间。

definition_en: a large heavy wild animal with thick fur, or to carry and endure
core_image: 一头厚毛的巨兽在雪地里慢慢走，脚下留下深深的印
scene: 雪后的林子里，一串很大的脚印通向树洞。A bear left deep prints across the snow.
sceneCN: 这里 bear 是「熊」（第 01 个义项）；句意是一只熊在雪地上留下深深的脚印。

pos.zh: 动词：承受、忍受、生育、带有

derivatives.zh: 由 bear 加 -able 构成，义为「可忍受的」
由 bear 加 -er 构成，义为「持票人、搬运者」
由 bear 与 skin 复合，义为「熊皮」

senses.title: The large heavy wild animal
senses.definition: a large wild animal with thick fur that walks on flat feet
senses.definitionCN: 体型大、毛厚、用平足行走的野生哺乳动物
senses.example: A bear left deep prints across the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 一只熊在雪地上留下深深的脚印。
senses.why: The noun bear goes back to Old English bera, 'the brown one', a name that replaced the animal's true name to avoid saying it aloud.
senses.whyCN: 名词 bear 来自古英语 bera「棕色的那个」，日耳曼人用颜色代称这种猛兽，以免直呼其名。

senses.title: To carry a heavy thing
senses.definition: to carry something heavy, or to hold weight
senses.definitionCN: 承担重量，或把重物带着走
senses.example: She bore the heavy box upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把沉重的箱子里搬上了楼。
senses.why: The verb bear comes from Old English beran, 'to carry', and its oldest work is carrying a load on the body.
senses.whyCN: 动词 bear 来自古英语 beran「携带」，最古老的任务就是用身体扛着东西走。

senses.title: To endure something hard
senses.definition: to suffer or accept something difficult without giving way
senses.definitionCN: 艰难之事压在身上而不垮掉
senses.example: I can't bear the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 我受不了这噪音。
senses.why: If a body can carry a heavy load, it can also carry pain or noise; 'carrying' becomes 'enduring'.
senses.whyCN: 身体扛得住重物，也就能扛住疼痛和噪音；「承载」于是变成「忍受」。

senses.title: To give birth to a child
senses.definition: to give birth to a child
senses.definitionCN: 生下孩子
senses.example: She bore a son in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她在春天生下了一个儿子。
senses.why: A mother carries the child inside her before birth, so the 'carrying' verb naturally came to mean giving birth.
senses.whyCN: 母亲在生出孩子之前先把他带在身上，所以这个「承载」的动词自然引申为生育。

senses.title: To show or have a mark or name
senses.definition: to have a mark, name or sign on it
senses.definitionCN: 上面带着印记、名字或标志
senses.example: The letter bears no signature.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信没有署名。
senses.why: Paper carries ink the way a body carries a load, so bear also means having a mark or name written on something.
senses.whyCN: 纸承载着墨迹，就像身体承载着重物，所以 bear 也表示某物上带着标记或名字。

intro.en: The history of bear is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bear 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Bera meant the animal, from a root for brown.
items.cn: 古英语 bera 指这种动物，词根意为褐色。

items.en: Germanic *berô is behind German Bär and Dutch beer.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *berô 也衍生出德语 Bär 与荷兰语 beer。

items.en: The animal was often called 'the brown one' to avoid its true name.
items.cn: 人们常用「棕色者」代称它，以避开真名。

items.en: The verb beran meant to carry, and developed the sense of enduring.
items.cn: 动词 beran 意为携带，后来发展出「忍受」义。

items.en: Bear covers the animal, carrying, endurance and birth.
items.cn: 现代英语中 bear 覆盖动物、承载、忍受与生育。

definition_en: for the reason that, introducing a cause
core_image: 两根线头一接，灯就亮了，原因和结果连在一起
scene: 屋里的灯忽然亮了，孩子顺着线找过去，发现插头被接上了。We stayed inside because the rain was heavy.
sceneCN: 这里 because 是「因为（引导原因）」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们待在屋里，因为雨下得很大。

derivatives.zh: 由 because 与 of 构成的短语介词
because 的英式口语缩略

senses.title: For the reason that, before a clause
senses.definition: for the reason that, used before a clause with a subject and verb
senses.definitionCN: 引出带主语和谓语的原因从句
senses.example: We stayed inside because the rain was heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 我们待在屋里，因为雨下得很大。
senses.why: Because came from by cause, 'by the cause that'; the word joins a whole statement to the reason that produced it.
senses.whyCN: because 来自 by cause「由于这个原因」，它把一整句话接到产生它的原因上去。

senses.title: On account of, in because of before a noun
senses.titleCN: 由于（because of 后接名词）
senses.definition: on account of, used with of before a noun or pronoun
senses.definitionCN: 与 of 连用，后接名词或代词表示原因
senses.example: The game was cancelled because of the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛因为下雨取消了。
senses.why: With of added, because can no longer take a full clause and must point at a noun or pronoun, giving the shorter 'on account of' use.
senses.whyCN: 加上 of 之后，because 不能再带完整从句，只能指向一个名词或代词，于是有了简短的「由于」用法。

items.en: The phrase bi cause meant 'by cause', from cause.
items.cn: 中古英语短语 bi cause 意为「由于原因」，来自 cause。

items.en: Cause itself comes from Latin causa, a reason or legal case.
items.cn: cause 本身来自拉丁语 causa，指原因或案件。

items.en: The phrase contracted into the single conjunction because.
items.cn: 短语缩合成单一连词 because。

items.en: Because became the standard word for introducing a cause.
items.cn: 现代英语中 because 成为引出原因的标准词。

items.en: Some teachers discourage starting a sentence with because in formal writing.
items.cn: 有些老师不鼓励在正式写作中以 because 开头。

definition_en: a room used for sleeping
core_image: 一间屋里床靠墙摆着，窗帘拉上一半
scene: 夜深了，家里只剩一间屋还透出一点光。The children share a bedroom upstairs.
sceneCN: 这里 bedroom 是「卧室」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们在楼上共用一间卧室。

derivatives.zh: 由本词前一成分独立成词，义为「床」
带卧室的，由 bedroom 加 -ed 构成

senses.title: A room used for sleeping
senses.definition: a room in a house or hotel used for sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 住宅或旅馆里供睡觉的房间
senses.example: The children share a bedroom upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在楼上共用一间卧室。
senses.why: Bedroom joins bed and room, and its whole meaning is the room built around a bed.
senses.whyCN: bedroom 由 bed 和 room 合成，意思就是围着床布置的那间屋。

senses.title: Used before a noun, meaning 'for a bedroom'
senses.definition: placed before another noun to mean 'used in or for a bedroom'
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示用在卧室里的
senses.example: She bought a small bedroom lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一盏卧室用的小灯。
senses.why: English lets a noun stand in front of another noun like an adjective, so bedroom in bedroom lamp marks the room the lamp belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以让名词像形容词一样站在另一名词前，于是 bedroom lamp 里的 bedroom 指明这盏灯属于哪个房间。

items.cn: bedroom 由 bed 与 room 复合，十六世纪有记录。

items.en: Bed comes from Old English bedd, a sleeping place.
items.cn: bed 来自古英语 bedd，指睡处。

items.en: Room comes from Old English rūm, meaning space.
items.cn: room 来自古英语 rūm，意为空间。

items.en: The compound names the private sleeping room of a home.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个复合词指住宅里的私人睡房。

items.en: It also covers hotel rooms and bedroom furniture.
items.cn: 它还覆盖旅馆客房与卧室家具。

definition_zh: 牛肉；抱怨（口语）；加强（口语）
definition_en: the meat of a cow, or an informal word for a complaint
core_image: 案板上切开的深红肉块，刀口还带着一点油光
scene: 灶上的锅盖一掀，炖了一下午的肉香漫进屋子。She cooked beef with potatoes for dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 beef 是「牛肉」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她晚饭做了土豆炖牛肉。

derivatives.zh: 由 beef 加 -y 构成，义为「结实的」
由 beef 与 steak 复合，义为「牛排」

senses.title: The meat of cattle
senses.definition: the meat of a cow or bull, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 牛身上可供食用的肉
senses.example: She cooked beef with potatoes for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她晚饭做了土豆炖牛肉。
senses.why: Beef came from Old French buef, 'ox', and in English it narrowed from the living animal to its meat on the table.
senses.whyCN: beef 来自古法语 buef「牛」，进入英语后从活着的牲畜收窄为端上桌的牛肉。

senses.title: An informal complaint
senses.definition: a reason for complaining, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指心里的不满或意见
senses.example: He has a beef about the noise next door.
senses.exampleCN: 他对隔壁的噪音有意见。
senses.why: American slang gave beef the sense of a grievance, so in informal talk the word now names a complaint rather than meat.
senses.whyCN: 美国俚语让 beef 带上了「不满」的意思，所以在口语里它指抱怨而不是肉。

senses.title: To make something stronger, in beef up
senses.definition: to strengthen or increase something, in the phrase beef up
senses.definitionCN: 在 beef up 中表示把某物加厚、加强
senses.example: They beefed up the team before the final.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛前他们加强了队伍。
senses.why: Beef up first meant feeding cattle to put on flesh, and the picture of added bulk carried over to strengthening anything.
senses.whyCN: beef up 原指把牛喂肥长肉，这份「加厚」的画面后来用到加强任何事物上。

items.en: Old French bueuf meant an ox and reached English as beef.
items.cn: 古法语 bueuf 指牛，进入英语作 beef。

items.en: After the Norman conquest the cooked meat took the French name.
items.cn: 诺曼征服之后，做熟的肉采用了法语名称。

items.en: English cow named the animal, beef the meat on the table.
items.cn: 英语用 cow 指活牛，用 beef 指餐桌上的肉。

items.en: Beef extends to strength and complaint in slang.
items.cn: 现代英语中 beef 在俚语里扩展到力气与抱怨。

definition_en: at the back of something, or less advanced than expected
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最后，前面的影子都落在他脚边
scene: 队伍走远了，最后一个孩子还在系鞋带，落在后面。He ran behind the others all the way home.
sceneCN: 这里 behind 是「在……后面」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他一路跟在其他人后面跑回家。

derivatives.zh: 落后的，由 behind 与 hand 复合
幕后的，由 behind 与 scenes 复合

senses.title: At the back of something
senses.definition: in the place at the back of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在某人某物的后方
senses.example: He ran behind the others all the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 他一路跟在其他人后面跑回家。
senses.why: Behind goes back to Old English behindan, be- plus hindan, 'from the back', so a rear position is its oldest meaning.
senses.whyCN: behind 来自古英语 behindan，由 be- 加 hindan「从后面」构成，后方位置是它最古老的意思。

senses.title: Less advanced, or late
senses.definition: less advanced than others, or later than planned
senses.definitionCN: 比别人进展慢，或晚于预定时间
senses.example: The train was ten minutes behind.
senses.exampleCN: 火车晚了十分钟。
senses.why: Someone who walks at the back of the group also falls behind in time, so the space word came to mark lateness and slower progress.
senses.whyCN: 走在队伍后面的人，时间上也落在后头，于是这个空间词开始标记迟到和进度落后。

senses.title: Giving support to someone
senses.definition: supporting or approving of someone
senses.definitionCN: 站在某人一边，给予支持
senses.example: The whole team is behind the new coach.
senses.exampleCN: 全队都支持新教练。
senses.why: To stand behind a person is to place your weight at his back, and that posture became the picture of giving support.
senses.whyCN: 站在一个人身后，就是把自己的力量放在他背后，这个姿势后来成了「给予支持」的画面。

senses.title: Hidden as the cause of something
senses.definition: hidden and forming the real cause of something
senses.definitionCN: 隐藏在表面之下，构成事情的真正原因
senses.example: What is behind the sudden decision?
senses.exampleCN: 这个突然的决定背后是什么原因？
senses.why: What is kept behind the curtain cannot be seen from the front, so behind also names the hidden reason of an event.
senses.whyCN: 藏在幕布后面的东西从正面看不见，所以 behind 也指事情隐藏起来的原因。

items.cn: 古英语 behindan 意为「从后面、在后面」。

items.cn: 这个词由 be- 与表示「后部」的词组合。

items.cn: 中古英语 behind 兼有位置在后与落后之义。

items.en: Behind extends to support, cause and schedule.
items.cn: 现代英语中 behind 扩展到支持、原因与时间。

definition_zh: 在……旁边；与……相比；（beside oneself）失控
definition_en: next to something, or in comparison with something
core_image: 一把椅子紧挨着另一把，扶手几乎碰到一起
scene: 等人时，她把包放在旁边的空座上，眼睛一直看着门口。She sat beside the window and waited.
sceneCN: 这里 beside 是「在……旁边」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她坐在窗边等着。

derivatives.zh: 由 beside 加 -s 构成，义为「此外」
习语，义为「情绪失控」

senses.title: Next to something
senses.definition: at the side of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 紧挨着某人某物的一侧
senses.example: She sat beside the window and waited.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边等着。
senses.why: Beside is Old English be sīdan, 'by the side', and the word still means exactly that: at a person's or thing's side.
senses.whyCN: beside 是古英语 be sīdan「在侧边」，至今仍是这个意思：在某人某物的一侧。

senses.title: Compared with something
senses.definition: when compared with someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 拿来做比较时，与某人某物对照
senses.example: Beside his brother, he is very tall.
senses.exampleCN: 和他弟弟相比，他个子很高。
senses.why: Place two people side by side and their difference becomes visible, so beside also means 'in comparison with'.
senses.whyCN: 把两个人并排放在一起，高下立刻看得出来，所以 beside 也表示「与……相比」。

senses.title: Out of control, in beside oneself
senses.definition: in a state of strong emotion, in the phrase beside oneself
senses.definitionCN: 在 beside oneself 中表示情绪激动到不能自持
senses.example: She was beside herself with worry.
senses.exampleCN: 她担心得六神无主。
senses.why: To be beside oneself is to stand outside yourself, as if your feelings had pushed you out of your own body.
senses.whyCN: beside oneself 字面是「站在自己旁边」，好像情绪把人挤出了自己的身体，因此指不能自持。

definition_en: of the highest quality, or in the most excellent way
core_image: 一排东西摆开，最亮的那一件被挑出来放在最前面
scene: 比赛结束，评委把三件作品排成一排，指着最亮的那件点头。This is the best cake I have ever tasted.
sceneCN: 这里 best 是「最好的」（第 01 个义项）；句意这是我吃过的最好吃的蛋糕。

derivatives.zh: best 的口语叠加形式，儿童用语
由 best 与 man 复合，义为「伴郎」

senses.title: Of the highest quality, superlative of good
senses.definition: better than all others, the superlative of good
senses.definitionCN: 好过所有其他，good 的最高级
senses.example: This is the best cake I have ever tasted.
senses.exampleCN: 这是我吃过的最好吃的蛋糕。
senses.why: Best is the superlative of good, from Old English betst beside bet, 'better'; it marks the top of a comparison.
senses.whyCN: best 是 good 的最高级，古英语 betst 与 bet「更好」同源，标出比较中的顶点。

senses.title: Most well, superlative of well
senses.definition: in the best way, the superlative of well
senses.definitionCN: 以最好的方式，well 的最高级
senses.example: She sings best in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她早晨唱得最好。
senses.why: The same superlative can also describe how an action is done, so best works as an adverb meaning 'most well'.
senses.whyCN: 同一个最高级也能描述动作做得怎样，所以 best 可作副词，表示「最好地」。

senses.title: The best person or thing
senses.definition: the best person or thing, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 作名词，指最好的人或事物
senses.example: He wants the best for his children.
senses.exampleCN: 他想给孩子最好的。
senses.why: Drop the noun after the adjective and best stands alone, taking over the whole phrase as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 把形容词后面的名词省掉，best 就单独站立，接管整个短语，成为名词。

items.en: Germanic *batistaz is behind German best and Dutch best.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 *batistaz 也衍生出德语 best 与荷兰语 best。

items.en: Best belongs to the same suppletive set as better and good.

items.en: The form became best and kept the superlative sense.
items.cn: 中古英语时期形式变为 best，保留最高级义。

items.en: Best also works as adverb, noun and in fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语中 best 还作副词、名词并见于固定短语。

definition_en: in the space or time separating two things, or shared by two sides
core_image: 两把椅子中间留出一条窄缝，人侧身通过
scene: 桌子两侧各坐一人，中间放着一壶茶。The shop is between the school and the park.
sceneCN: 这里 between 是「在两者之间」（第 01 个义项）；句意是那家店在学校和公园之间。

derivatives.zh: 由 between 加 -ness 构成，义为「介于两者之间的性质」
由 in 与 between 复合，义为「中间的」

senses.title: In the space separating two things
senses.definition: in the space that separates two places or things
senses.definitionCN: 处在两个地点或物体中间的空隙
senses.example: The shop is between the school and the park.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店在学校和公园之间。
senses.why: Between comes from Old English betweonum, be- plus tweonum, 'by two each'; its literal picture is one thing standing in the middle of two others.
senses.whyCN: between 来自古英语 betweonum，由 be- 加 tweonum「各两个」构成，字面画面就是一样东西立在另两样之间。

senses.title: In the period separating two times
senses.definition: in the period that separates two points in time
senses.definitionCN: 处在两个时间点中间的那一段
senses.example: The shop is open between nine and five.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店九点到五点之间营业。
senses.why: A stretch of time has two ends just as a road has two banks, so the space word also marks the interval from one hour to another.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间也有两个端点，就像道路有两岸，所以这个空间词也用来标出两个钟点之间的那一段。

senses.title: In the relationship of two or more people
senses.definition: used of a relationship or connection involving two or more people
senses.definitionCN: 用于两个或更多人之间的关系与联系
senses.example: There is a strong friendship between them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们之间有很深的友谊。
senses.why: A friendship does not sit on either person; it runs in the space joining them, which is exactly where between puts it.
senses.whyCN: 友谊并不落在任何一个人身上，而是跑在连接两人的那段空间里，between 正是把它放在那里。

senses.title: Shared out among two or more
senses.definition: divided or shared among two or more people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 在两个或更多人、群体之间分开或共享
senses.example: They divided the money between the two of them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把钱在两人之间分了。
senses.why: When something is split, each share comes out of the space separating the receivers, so between also marks how a whole is shared.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西被分开时，每一份都出自接受者之间的那块空间，所以 between 也标记整体怎样分配。

definition_en: a feathered animal that can usually fly, or informally a person
core_image: 一只小东西落在枝头，羽毛蓬起，喉咙发出短促的鸣叫
scene: 清晨窗外，一只小东西在枝头跳了两下，叫了一声。A bird sang outside my window.
sceneCN: 这里 bird 是「鸟」（第 01 个义项）；句意是一只鸟在我窗外鸣叫。

derivatives.zh: 由 bird 加 -ie 构成，义为「小鸟」
由 bird 与 watching 复合，义为「观鸟」
由 bird 与 cage 复合，义为「鸟笼」

senses.title: A feathered animal with wings
senses.definition: a warm-blooded animal with feathers and wings, usually able to fly
senses.definitionCN: 有羽毛和翅膀、通常会飞的温血动物
senses.example: A bird sang outside my window.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鸟在我窗外鸣叫。
senses.why: Bird comes from Old English bridd, first used of young nestlings and later of the whole feathered kind.
senses.whyCN: bird 来自古英语 bridd，最初指巢里的雏鸟，后来扩大到所有有羽毛的鸟类。

senses.title: An odd or unusual person, in informal talk
senses.definition: a person, especially an odd or unusual one, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指人，尤指古怪特别的人
senses.example: He is a funny old bird.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个古怪的老头。
senses.why: Calling a person a bird borrows the creature's odd habits and quick movements, so the word can label a peculiar character.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作 bird，是借鸟的古怪习性和灵活动作来打比方，于是这个词能指性格特别的人。

senses.title: Someone who acts early, in early bird
senses.definition: a person who arrives or acts early, in the phrase early bird
senses.definitionCN: 在 early bird 中指起得早、到得早的人
senses.example: The early birds got the best seats.
senses.exampleCN: 早到的人坐到了最好的位置。
senses.why: Birds sing before sunrise, so an early bird became the picture of anyone who is first on the scene.
senses.whyCN: 鸟在日出前就鸣叫，于是 early bird 成了「最早到场的人」的画面。

intro.en: The history of bird is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: bird 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Bridd first meant a young bird.
items.cn: 古英语 bridd 最初指幼鸟。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic group for young creatures.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语中表示幼小生物的一组词。

items.en: Fugol was the older general word for birds.
items.cn: fugol 是更早的鸟类泛称。

items.en: Bridd became bird and widened to all birds.
items.cn: bridd 变为 bird，并扩展到所有鸟类。

items.en: Bird replaced fowl in everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语中 bird 在日常使用中取代了 fowl。

items.en: Bird also means a person or an aircraft informally.
items.cn: 俚语中 bird 还可指人或飞机。

definition_en: a dark board on which writing is done with chalk
core_image: 一块深绿色的板子立在墙前，上面留着擦了又写的粉笔痕
scene: 教室里粉笔灰落在讲台边，老师转身在板上写下一个词。The teacher wrote the date on the blackboard.
sceneCN: 这里 blackboard 是「黑板」（第 01 个义项）；句意是老师在黑板上写下日期。

derivatives.zh: 由 blackboard 与 eraser 复合，义为「黑板擦」
由 blackboard 与 paint 复合，义为「黑板漆」
本词后一成分独立成词，义为「板」

senses.title: A dark board for writing with chalk
senses.definition: a dark smooth board on which teachers write with chalk
senses.definitionCN: 教师用粉笔写字的深色光滑板面
senses.example: The teacher wrote the date on the blackboard.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在黑板上写下了日期。
senses.why: Blackboard is black plus board, a board made black so that white chalk shows up on it.
senses.whyCN: blackboard 就是 black 加 board，把板子做成黑色，白粉笔写上去才看得清。

senses.title: A dark board showing prices or notices in public
senses.definition: a dark board on which a shop or venue writes prices or notices
senses.definitionCN: 店铺或场所用来写价目、告示的深色板子
senses.example: The day's prices were written on a blackboard outside the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 当天的价目写在店外的黑板上。
senses.why: The same dark board moved from the classroom to the shop door and now carries prices and notices, which is a separate everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 同一块深色板子从教室挪到店门口，写上了价目和告示，这就成了另一种日常用法。

items.en: Blackboard joins black and board.
items.cn: blackboard 由 black 与 board 复合。

items.en: Black comes from Old English blæc.
items.cn: black 来自古英语 blæc。

items.en: Board comes from Old English bord, a plank.
items.cn: board 来自古英语 bord，指木板。

items.en: The compound became the standard classroom writing board.
items.cn: 这个复合词成为教室书写板的标准说法。

items.en: It also names interactive boards and blackboard paint.
items.cn: 现代英语中它还指互动板与黑板漆。

definition_en: a small vessel for travelling on water
core_image: 一只窄木船系在岸边，船底轻轻拍着水
scene: 湖边的木栈桥旁，一条小船随着水波轻轻晃动。We rowed the boat across the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 boat 是「小船」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们划船穿过湖面。

derivatives.zh: 由 boat 加 -ing 构成，义为「划船」
由 boat 与 man 复合，义为「船夫」
由 boat 与 yard 复合，义为「造船厂」

senses.title: A small craft that travels on water
senses.definition: a small vehicle built to carry people or goods on water
senses.definitionCN: 在水上载人或载货的小型交通工具
senses.example: We rowed the boat across the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们划船穿过湖面。
senses.why: Boat goes back to Old English bāt, a small wooden craft moved by oars or sail.
senses.whyCN: boat 来自古英语 bāt，指靠桨或帆驱动的小型木船。

senses.title: A ship, as a way of travelling
senses.definition: a ship or large vessel, especially when naming the way one travels
senses.definitionCN: 泛指船只，尤用于说明出行的方式
senses.example: They went to the island by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们乘船去了岛上。
senses.why: In everyday travel talk boat covers any vessel, so 'by boat' names a means of transport rather than a particular small craft.
senses.whyCN: 在日常出行的话里，boat 泛指任何船，所以 by boat 说的是交通方式，而不是某条小船。

senses.title: To travel or row in a boat
senses.definition: to travel on water in a boat, or to row one
senses.definitionCN: 乘船在水上行进，或划动船只
senses.example: They boated down the river all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个下午都乘船顺河而下。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without changing shape, so boat simply names the activity of moving by boat.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接转成动词，字形不变，boat 于是表示「乘船、划船」这个动作。

items.en: Boat covers small craft and the verb to travel by boat.

definition_zh: 划船；乘船游玩；划船运动
definition_en: the activity of travelling in a small boat for pleasure
core_image: 阳光下的湖面，一只小船被桨推开，水纹一圈圈散开
scene: 周末的湖上，一家人把船推下水，桨声惊起岸边的鸟。Boating is popular on this lake in summer.
sceneCN: 这里 boating 是「划船活动」（第 01 个义项）；句意是夏天这个湖上流行划船游玩。

derivatives.zh: 本词的主词，义为「船」
由 boating 改写而来，义为「划船者」
由 boating 与 lake 复合，义为「划船湖」

senses.title: The pastime of going out on the water in a boat
senses.definition: the activity of taking a boat on the water for pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 把船推下水、在水上消遣的活动
senses.example: Boating is popular on this lake in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天这个湖上流行划船游玩。
senses.why: Boating is boat plus -ing, naming the activity itself: pushing off and spending time on the water.
senses.whyCN: boating 是 boat 加 -ing，指这项活动本身：把船推下水，在水上消磨时光。

senses.title: The sport of rowing or sailing in competition
senses.definition: the sport of rowing or sailing boats, often in races
senses.definitionCN: 有规则、常以比赛形式进行的划船或帆船运动
senses.example: She took up boating at school and now races for the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校开始划船，现在为俱乐部参赛。
senses.why: The same activity, once it has rules, crews and races, becomes a sport, and boating is the name used for that side of it.
senses.whyCN: 同样的活动一旦有了规则、船员和比赛，就成了体育项目，boating 正是指这一面。

intro.en: The history of boating is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: boating 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Boating is boat plus the -ing suffix.
items.cn: boating 由 boat 加 -ing 构成。

items.en: Boat comes from Old English bāt, a small vessel.
items.cn: boat 来自古英语 bāt，指小船。

items.en: The suffix turns the noun into an activity noun.
items.cn: 这个后缀把名词变成活动名词。

items.en: The word names leisure boating and the sport.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词指休闲划船与划船运动。

items.en: It also covers boating gear and boating accidents.
items.cn: 它还覆盖划船装备与划船事故。

definition_zh: 身体；尸体；主体；团体；大量
definition_en: the whole physical frame of a person or animal, or the main part of something
core_image: 一个人站在镜前，从肩到脚连成完整的轮廓
scene: 镜子里，一个人的轮廓从肩头一直延伸到脚踝。Exercise keeps the body strong.
sceneCN: 这里 body 是「身体」（第 01 个义项）；句意是运动让身体保持强壮。

derivatives.zh: 由 body 加 -ly 构成，义为「身体的」
由 any 与 body 复合，义为「任何人」
由 body 与 work 复合，义为「车身」

senses.title: The whole physical frame of a person or animal
senses.definition: the whole physical structure of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物从肩到脚的整个躯体
senses.example: Exercise keeps the body strong.
senses.exampleCN: 运动让身体保持强壮。
senses.why: Body comes from Old English bodig, 'trunk', the main frame of a living creature.
senses.whyCN: body 来自古英语 bodig「躯干」，指一个活物最主要的那副骨架与肉身。

senses.title: A dead person's remains
senses.definition: the remains of a dead person
senses.definitionCN: 人死之后留下的躯体
senses.example: The body was found near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 尸体在河边被发现。
senses.why: What is left after death is still the same frame, so body also names a corpse without any change of shape.
senses.whyCN: 人死后留下的仍是那副躯体，所以 body 不用改变字形也能指尸体。

senses.title: The main part of something, apart from its ends
senses.definition: the main part of an object or document, apart from its ends
senses.definitionCN: 物体或文件去掉头尾之后的主要部分
senses.example: The body of the letter explained the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 信的主体部分解释了这个计划。
senses.why: A letter or a car has a main middle section the way a creature has a trunk, so the trunk word lends itself to the main part of things.
senses.whyCN: 一封信、一辆车也有像躯干那样的中段主体，于是这个指躯干的词被借去称呼事物的主要部分。

senses.title: An organised group of people
senses.definition: a group of people organised for a purpose, such as a council
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的组织起来的一群人，如理事会
senses.example: The school's governing body meets in May.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的理事会五月开会。
senses.why: People joined under one set of rules form a single whole, like a body with many limbs, so body also means an organised group.
senses.whyCN: 一群人按同一套章程聚成一个整体，就像有多条肢体的身躯，所以 body 也指有组织的团体。

senses.title: A large amount of something collected
senses.definition: a large amount of material or information of one kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类材料或信息聚成的大宗
senses.example: There is a body of evidence against him.
senses.exampleCN: 有大量证据对他不利。
senses.why: Many separate pieces gathered into one mass look like a single body, which is why body can mean a large collected amount.
senses.whyCN: 许多分散的材料堆成一团，看起来就像一个整体，所以 body 可以表示聚集起来的大量事物。

intro.cn: body 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: The oldest sense was the trunk, later the whole frame.
items.cn: 最早的义项是躯干，后来指整个身体。

items.en: Body widened to persons, groups and main parts.
items.cn: 中古英语中 body 扩展到人、群体与主体部分。

items.en: Body covers corpses, organisations and physical objects.
items.cn: 现代英语中 body 覆盖尸体、组织与物理物体。

definition_en: a container with a narrow neck for holding liquids

senses.example: He opened a bottle of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开了一瓶水。
senses.why: Bottle came from Old French boteille, from Latin butticula, 'small container', and the narrow-necked shape is still central.
senses.whyCN: bottle 来自古法语 boteille，源头是拉丁语 butticula「小容器」，细颈的形状至今仍是它的核心。

senses.title: The amount a bottle holds
senses.definition: the amount of liquid that a bottle contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只瓶子所装的液体分量
senses.example: They drank a whole bottle between them.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一起喝完了整整一瓶。
senses.why: English often lets the container stand for its contents, so a bottle can mean one bottleful.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让容器代替它装的东西，所以 a bottle 也能指「一瓶的量」。

senses.title: To put liquid into bottles
senses.definition: to fill bottles with a liquid, usually in a factory
senses.definitionCN: 把液体装进瓶子，通常在工厂里进行
senses.example: The factory bottles milk every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂每天早上给牛奶装瓶。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so bottle names the act of filling a bottle.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，bottle 就表示往瓶子里装东西这个动作。

senses.title: To feed a baby or young animal with a bottle
senses.definition: to feed a baby or young animal from a bottle
senses.definitionCN: 用奶瓶给婴儿或幼崽喂奶
senses.example: She bottle-fed the lamb every two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她每两小时用奶瓶喂一次小羊。
senses.why: When a baby is fed from a bottle instead of the breast, the verb bottle names that way of feeding.
senses.whyCN: 当婴儿不是吃母乳而是用奶瓶时，动词 bottle 就指这种喂养方式。

items.cn: 拉丁语 buttis 指桶或容器。

items.en: Old French botele carried the word to English.
items.cn: 古法语 botele 把这个词带入英语。

items.en: Bottle first named leather and glass vessels.
items.cn: 中古英语中 bottle 先指皮革与玻璃容器。

items.en: Glass bottles became everyday containers.
items.cn: 现代英语中玻璃瓶成为日常容器。

items.en: The verb means to store or to feed from a bottle.
items.cn: 动词义指装瓶存放或用奶瓶喂养。

items.en: Bottle also means courage in British slang.
items.cn: 英式俚语中 bottle 还指勇气。

definition_zh: 碗；一碗之量；碗状物；保龄球
definition_en: a round deep dish for food, or the amount it holds
core_image: 一只圆口浅底的碗放在桌上，热气从里面升起来
scene: 桌上摆着一只白瓷圆碗，里面盛着汤。She served the soup in a bowl.
sceneCN: 这里 bowl 是「碗」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她把汤盛在碗里。

pos.zh: 名词：碗、一碗之量、碗状物

由 bowl 加 -er 构成，义为「投球手」

senses.title: A round deep dish for food
senses.definition: a round, deep dish used for food or liquid
senses.definitionCN: 盛食物或汤水的圆形深盘
senses.example: She served the soup in a bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她把汤盛在碗里。
senses.why: Bowl comes from Old English bolla, 'a round vessel', and the round hollow shape is the heart of the word.
senses.whyCN: bowl 来自古英语 bolla「圆形器皿」，圆形凹陷的形状正是这个词的核心。

senses.title: The amount a bowl holds
senses.definition: the amount of food that a bowl contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只碗所盛的食物分量
senses.example: He ate a bowl of rice.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃了一碗米饭。
senses.why: As with bottle, the container can name one bowlful, so a bowl of rice means the amount inside.
senses.whyCN: 和 bottle 一样，容器名也能代指一碗的量，所以 a bowl of rice 说的是里面的分量。

senses.title: A rounded part shaped like a bowl
senses.definition: a rounded hollow part of an object, shaped like a bowl
senses.definitionCN: 物体上像碗一样的圆形凹陷部分
senses.example: The bowl of the old pipe was black with soot.
senses.exampleCN: 旧烟斗的斗钵被烟灰熏黑了。
senses.why: Anything hollowed into the same round curve borrows the name, so the bowl of a pipe or a toilet is still a bowl.
senses.whyCN: 任何掏成同样圆凹形状的部分都借用了这个名字，所以烟斗的斗钵、马桶的盆都叫 bowl。

senses.title: To roll or throw a ball in a game
senses.definition: to roll or throw a ball toward a target in cricket or bowling
senses.definitionCN: 在板球或保龄球里把球投向目标
senses.example: He bowled the first over of the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他投出了比赛的第一轮球。
senses.why: The verb bowl comes from the rolling action in bowling, where the ball travels down a lane toward a target.
senses.whyCN: 动词 bowl 来自保龄球里滚球的动作，球沿着球道滚向目标。

definition_zh: 盒子；箱；一盒之量；方框；拳击
definition_en: a container with flat sides, or to fight with the fists
core_image: 一只纸盒盖上盖子，四角压平，里面装着零碎的东西
scene: 柜子里堆着几只纸盒，最上面那只贴着标签。She put the gift in a box.
sceneCN: 这里 box 是「盒子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她把礼物装进一个盒子。

derivatives.zh: 由 box 加 -ing 构成，义为「拳击」
由 box 加 -er 构成，义为「拳击手」
由 box 加 -ful 构成，义为「一盒之量」

senses.title: A container with flat sides
senses.definition: a container with flat sides, usually with a lid
senses.definitionCN: 有平整侧面、通常带盖的容器
senses.example: She put the gift in a box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把礼物装进一个盒子。
senses.why: Box came through Latin buxis, 'boxwood container', and the square wooden case gave the word its shape-filled meaning.
senses.whyCN: box 经拉丁语 buxis「黄杨木盒」而来，方正的木匣给了这个词带形状的含义。

senses.title: The amount a box holds
senses.definition: the amount of something that a box contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只盒子所装的分量
senses.example: He bought a box of chocolates for her.
senses.exampleCN: 他给她买了一盒巧克力。
senses.why: The container again stands for its contents, so a box of chocolates means one boxful.
senses.whyCN: 容器又一次代替内容物，所以 a box of chocolates 指的是一盒的分量。

senses.title: A square drawn on a form
senses.definition: a square or rectangle printed on a form for a mark
senses.definitionCN: 表格上印好的、用来打勾的方框
senses.example: Tick the box beside your name.
senses.exampleCN: 在你名字旁边的方框里打勾。
senses.why: A printed square looks exactly like the top of a box, so the shape word was extended to the squares on forms.
senses.whyCN: 表格上印的方框看起来就像盒子的顶面，于是这个形状词扩展到表格里的方格。

senses.title: To fight with the fists as a sport
senses.definition: to fight someone with the fists, following the rules of boxing
senses.definitionCN: 按拳击规则用拳头与人搏斗
senses.example: He boxed for the school team.
senses.exampleCN: 他为校队打拳击。
senses.why: The verb box means 'to strike with the fist'; it happens to share its spelling with the container word but belongs to a different line of use.
senses.whyCN: 动词 box 意为「用拳头打」，它与表示容器的 box 拼写相同，但属于另一支用法。

intro.en: The history of box is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: box 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Buxis meant a box made of boxwood.
items.cn: 拉丁语 buxis 指黄杨木做的盒子。

items.en: Greek pyxis meant a box with a lid.
items.cn: 希腊语 pyxis 指带盖的盒子。

items.en: Box entered English from Latin.
items.cn: box 经由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The word extended to any square container.

definition_en: a male child or a young man
core_image: 一个短发少年蹲在门口，手里握着一只刚捡到的球
scene: 门口蹲着一个短发少年，手里转着一只球。The boy ran across the field.
sceneCN: 这里 boy 是「男孩」（第 01 个义项）；句意是那个男孩跑过田野。

derivatives.zh: 由 boy 加 -ish 构成，义为「男孩气的」
由 boy 与 friend 复合，义为「男朋友」
由 school 与 boy 复合，义为「男学生」

senses.title: A male child
senses.definition: a young male person
senses.definitionCN: 年纪小的男性
senses.example: The boy ran across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 那个男孩跑过田野。
senses.why: Boy came into Middle English as boi, 'a young male', and that age limit is still its centre.
senses.whyCN: boy 以中古英语 boi「年少的男性」进入英语，年龄界限至今仍是它的核心。

senses.title: Someone's son
senses.definition: a person's son, seen as belonging to the family
senses.definitionCN: 某人的儿子，从家庭归属来说
senses.example: Their boy is at university now.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的儿子现在上大学了。
senses.why: Parents say my boy or their boy when the young male is their own son, so the family link became part of the sense.
senses.whyCN: 父母说 my boy、their boy 时，指的是自己的儿子，于是家庭关系也进入了这个词的意思。

senses.title: A young man, in informal talk
senses.definition: a young man, used informally among friends or in a team
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指年轻男子，常用在伙伴或队伍之间
senses.example: The boys on the team meet every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 队里的小伙子们每周五聚会。
senses.why: Among adults the word drops its age limit and becomes a friendly label for a young man, especially one of the group.
senses.whyCN: 在成年人之间，这个词放开了年龄限制，成了对年轻男子的亲切称呼，尤其指自己一伙里的人。

definition_en: a food made from flour and baked, or the money needed to live
core_image: 一只刚出炉的圆面包放在木板上，表皮鼓起，裂缝里冒着热气
scene: 厨房里，刚出炉的面包放在木板上，表皮还在轻轻作响。She bought a loaf of bread.
sceneCN: 这里 bread 是「面包」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她买了一条面包。

derivatives.zh: 由 bread 与 crumbs 复合，义为「面包屑」
由 bread 与 winner 复合，义为「养家糊口的人」
由 bread 与 board 复合，义为「切面包板」

senses.title: Food made from baked flour
senses.definition: a food made by baking a dough of flour and water
senses.definitionCN: 面粉加水揉成面团后烤成的食物
senses.example: She bought a loaf of bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一条面包。
senses.why: Bread goes back to Old English brēad, 'a piece of food', which narrowed over the centuries to baked flour food.
senses.whyCN: bread 来自古英语 brēad「一块食物」，几个世纪里词义收窄，专指面粉烤成的食物。

senses.title: The money needed to live
senses.definition: the money one earns in order to live
senses.definitionCN: 维持生活所需的收入
senses.example: He works hard to earn his bread.
senses.exampleCN: 他努力工作挣饭吃。
senses.why: Bread was the everyday food that kept a family alive, so earning one's bread came to mean earning a living.
senses.whyCN: 面包是养活一家人的日常主食，所以 earn one's bread 就指挣钱糊口。

senses.title: To coat food with breadcrumbs
senses.definition: to cover food with breadcrumbs before cooking
senses.definitionCN: 烹饪前给食物裹上一层碎面包屑
senses.example: She breaded the fish before frying it.
senses.exampleCN: 她把鱼裹上面包屑再煎。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so bread names the act of covering food with crushed bread.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，bread 表示给食物裹上碎面包这个动作。

definition_en: the first meal of the day, or to eat it
core_image: 清晨桌上摆着热牛奶、切片面包和一只剥了一半的蛋
scene: 天刚亮，厨房桌上已经摆好热牛奶和切片面包。We had breakfast before school.
sceneCN: 这里 breakfast 是「早餐」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们上学前吃了早餐。

derivatives.zh: 由 breakfast 加 -ed 构成，义为「吃过早餐的」
由 breakfast 加 -ing 构成，义为「吃早餐」
由 bed 与 breakfast 复合，义为「提供住宿与早餐的旅馆」

senses.title: The first meal of the day
senses.definition: the first meal of the day, eaten in the morning
senses.definitionCN: 一天中的第一顿饭，在早晨吃
senses.example: We had breakfast before school.
senses.exampleCN: 我们上学前吃了早餐。
senses.why: Breakfast joins break and fast: a fast is a period without food, so breakfast is the meal that breaks the night's fast.
senses.whyCN: breakfast 由 break 和 fast 合成；fast 指禁食的一段时间，breakfast 就是打破一夜禁食的那一餐。

senses.title: To eat breakfast
senses.definition: to eat the first meal of the day
senses.definitionCN: 吃一天中的第一顿饭
senses.example: They breakfasted on the terrace.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在露台上吃了早餐。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so breakfast simply names the act of eating that first meal.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，breakfast 就表示吃这一顿早饭的行为。

intro.en: The history of breakfast is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: breakfast 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Breakfast joins break and fast, meaning to end the night's fast.
items.cn: 中古英语 breakfast 由 break 与 fast 组合，意为结束一夜的禁食。

items.en: Break comes from Old English brecan.
items.cn: break 来自古英语 brecan。

items.en: Fast meant going without food.
items.cn: fast 指禁食。

items.en: The compound names the first meal and the verb.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个复合词指第一餐与吃早餐的动词。

items.en: It also names a meal provided by hotels.
items.cn: 它还指旅馆提供的早餐。

definition_en: a structure carrying a road over water, or to connect two sides
core_image: 一座石桥横跨河面，桥拱的影子落在水里
scene: 河两岸各有几户人家，中间一座石桥把路连起来。A stone bridge crosses the river.
sceneCN: 这里 bridge 是「桥」（第 01 个义项）；句意是一座石桥横跨这条河。

derivatives.zh: 由 bridge 加 -ing 构成，义为「桥接」
由 bridge 与 head 复合，义为「桥头堡」
由 draw 与 bridge 复合，义为「吊桥」

senses.title: A structure built over a river or road
senses.definition: a structure built over a river, road or railway so people can cross
senses.definitionCN: 架在河面或道路上方、供人通过的建筑物
senses.example: A stone bridge crosses the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一座石桥横跨河面。
senses.why: Bridge comes from Old English brycg, a raised way over water, and that crossing is still the word's base.
senses.whyCN: bridge 来自古英语 brycg，指架在水上的通道，这个「跨越」的意思至今是它的底子。

senses.title: Something that connects two sides
senses.definition: something that joins two separate things or groups
senses.definitionCN: 把两个分开的事物或群体接起来的东西
senses.example: The course is a bridge between school and work.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程是学校与工作之间的桥梁。
senses.why: A bridge joins two banks that would otherwise stay apart, so any connecting link between people or ideas borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 桥把本来隔开的两岸接起来，于是任何连接人或观念的纽带都借用了这个名字。

senses.title: A card game for four players
senses.definition: a card game for four players played in pairs
senses.definitionCN: 四人分两组进行的纸牌游戏
senses.example: They play bridge on Sunday evenings.
senses.exampleCN: 他们星期天晚上打桥牌。
senses.why: The card game called bridge shares the spelling of the structure word but comes from a separate line of card-game names.
senses.whyCN: 叫作 bridge 的纸牌游戏与表示桥梁的词拼写相同，但它来自另一支牌戏名称。

senses.title: To join two sides or close a gap
senses.definition: to build a bridge over something, or to close a gap between two sides
senses.definitionCN: 在两岸之间架桥，或把两方的差距接上
senses.example: The two sides bridged their differences.
senses.exampleCN: 两方弥合了分歧。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to bridge is to act as a bridge, whether over a river or across a disagreement.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词：bridge 就是充当桥，不论跨过河水还是跨过分歧。

items.cn: 古英语 brycġ 指桥。

items.en: The word is related to German Brücke.
items.cn: 这个词与德语 Brücke 同源。

items.en: The word spread to ship, nose and violin parts.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到舰桥、鼻梁与琴桥。

items.en: Bridge named a card game in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪 bridge 成为一种纸牌游戏的名字。

items.en: The verb means to span or to connect.
items.cn: 动词义指架桥跨越或连接双方。

definition_en: a structure with walls and a roof, or the act of constructing
core_image: 一栋楼从地面立起，窗子一层层往上排，像叠起的格子
scene: 街角那栋楼一层层往上排着窗子，傍晚灯一盏盏亮起。The new building has ten floors.

senses.title: A structure with walls and a roof
senses.definition: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or an office

senses.example: The new building has ten floors.

senses.why: Building is build plus -ing, and the ending can name the finished thing: what has been built.

senses.title: The act or process of constructing

senses.definitionCN: 把某物建起来的过程
senses.example: The building of the bridge took two years.

senses.why: The same -ing form also names the activity itself, so the building of a bridge is the work, not the finished bridge.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ing 形式也能指活动本身，所以 the building of a bridge 说的是施工，不是建成的桥。

senses.title: The construction industry

senses.example: He works in building.
senses.exampleCN: 他从事建筑业。
senses.why: Once the whole trade of putting up structures is treated as one field, building becomes the name of that industry.
senses.whyCN: 当建造房屋这一整行当被看成一个领域，building 就成了这个行业的名称。

definition_en: having much to do, full of activity, or in use
core_image: 一只手同时抓着电话、笔和一叠纸，桌上还排着待办的事
scene: 办公桌上电话响个不停，手里还攥着一叠没签完的纸。She is busy with her homework.
sceneCN: 这里 busy 是「忙的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她忙着做作业。

pos.zh: 形容词：忙的、繁忙的、占线的

derivatives.zh: 由 busy 的旧名词形式演变，义为「生意」
由 busy 加 -ly 构成，义为「忙碌地」

senses.title: Having a lot to do
senses.definition: having much work to do, with little free time
senses.definitionCN: 手头事情多、没有空闲
senses.example: She is busy with her homework.
senses.exampleCN: 她忙着做作业。
senses.why: Busy comes from Old English bisig, 'occupied, diligent', and its centre is a person who cannot put the work down.
senses.whyCN: busy 来自古英语 bisig「专心、操劳」，核心就是一个放不下手里事情的人。

senses.title: Full of activity
senses.definition: full of people or movement, used of places and times
senses.definitionCN: 形容地方或时段人来人往、活动不断
senses.example: They live on a busy street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在一条繁忙的街上。
senses.why: A place can be as occupied as a person: if people keep coming and going, the street itself is busy.
senses.whyCN: 地方也能像人一样「闲不下来」：人来人往不断，街道本身就 busy。

senses.title: In use, of a telephone line
senses.definition: already in use, said of a telephone line
senses.definitionCN: 电话线正被使用，打不进去
senses.example: The line is busy.
senses.exampleCN: 电话占线。
senses.why: A line that is occupied cannot take another call, so the same word for 'taken up' is used for the telephone.
senses.whyCN: 一条被占用的线接不进别的电话，于是表示「被占着」的同一个词用到了电话上。

senses.title: To keep oneself occupied
senses.definition: to keep oneself occupied with something
senses.definitionCN: 让自己一直有事情做
senses.example: She busied herself with the dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 她忙着洗碗。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb, so to busy oneself is to make oneself busy on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作动词，busy oneself 就是主动让自己忙起来。

items.en: The word spread to streets and telephone lines.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到街道与电话线。

items.en: Busy also means too curious about others.
items.cn: 现代英语中 busy 还指过分关心别人的事。

definition_en: used to introduce a contrast, or to mean except
core_image: 两句话之间画一道转折的弯线，前半句向左，后半句向右
scene: 天气预报说晴，门口却摆着一把湿透的伞。It was sunny, but the ground was wet.
sceneCN: 这里 but 是「但是」（第 01 个义项）；句意是天晴了，但地面还是湿的。

derivatives.zh: 由 but 与 for 构成的短语，义为「要不是」
由 all 与 but 构成的短语，义为「几乎」

senses.title: Introducing a contrast
senses.definition: used to introduce something that contrasts with what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 引出与上一句相反或不同的话
senses.example: It was sunny, but the ground was wet.
senses.exampleCN: 天晴了，但地面还是湿的。
senses.why: But came from Old English butan, 'outside, except'; setting the first statement aside and putting another in its place produced the contrast use.
senses.whyCN: but 来自古英语 butan「在……之外、除……以外」；把前一句搁到一边、换上另一句，就产生了转折用法。

senses.title: Except
senses.definition: except, leaving one person or thing out
senses.definitionCN: 把某一个或某一些排除在外
senses.example: Everyone but Tom came.
senses.exampleCN: 除了汤姆，大家都来了。
senses.why: The oldest sense of 'outside' survives here: everyone is counted, with Tom placed outside the group.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的「在外」义在这里保留下来：所有人都算上，只把汤姆放在群体之外。

senses.title: Only
senses.definition: only, when everything else is excluded
senses.definitionCN: 排除其余，只剩下一样
senses.example: He is nothing but a child.
senses.exampleCN: 他不过是个孩子。
senses.why: If everything else is pushed outside, what remains is 'nothing but', so the except word ends up meaning 'only'.
senses.whyCN: 把其余一切都推到外面，剩下的就是 nothing but，于是这个表示「除外」的词最终表示「只」。

items.cn: 古英语 butan 意为「在外、除……之外」。

items.en: The form became but and added the contrast sense.
items.cn: 中古英语中形式变为 but，并增加转折义。

items.en: The contrast use grew from the except sense.
items.cn: 转折用法从例外义发展而来。

definition_en: to get something by paying money, or informally to believe
core_image: 一只手把硬币放到柜台上，另一只手接过纸袋
scene: 柜台前，一枚硬币被推过去，一只纸袋递了回来。She bought a new coat yesterday.
sceneCN: 这里 buy 是「买」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她昨天买了一件新大衣。

pos.zh: 名词：购买、买得值的东西

derivatives.zh: 由 buy 加 -er 构成，义为「买家」
由 buy 加 -ing 构成，义为「购买」
由 buy 与 out 复合，义为「收购」

senses.title: To get something by paying money
senses.definition: to obtain something by paying money for it
senses.definitionCN: 付钱把东西换到手
senses.example: She bought a new coat yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 她昨天买了一件新大衣。
senses.why: Buy goes back to Old English bycgan, 'to get in exchange for payment', and the exchange is still the whole sense.
senses.whyCN: buy 来自古英语 bycgan「用钱换得」，这种交换至今就是它的全部意思。

senses.title: To believe or accept, in informal talk
senses.definition: to believe or accept an idea or story, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语里表示相信或接受某种说法
senses.example: I don't buy that story.
senses.exampleCN: 我不信那套说法。
senses.why: Informal English treats an idea as something offered for sale: if you accept it, you 'buy' it.
senses.whyCN: 口语把一种说法当成待售的货物：你接受了，就等于把它「买」了下来。

senses.title: A purchase, or something worth its price
senses.definition: a thing bought, or a purchase that was worth the money
senses.definitionCN: 买到的东西，或价钱划算的一次购买
senses.example: This bike was a good buy.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆自行车买得很值。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun, so buy names either the purchase or the thing that proved worth buying.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，buy 既可指一次购买，也可指买得划算的那件东西。

intro.cn: buy 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.cn: 古英语 bycgan 意为购买或付款取得。

items.cn: 古诺斯语与哥特语中有相关形式，但数量很少。

items.en: The past tense bought took shape in Middle English.
items.cn: 过去式 bought 在中古英语定型。

items.en: Buy extends to belief and a good bargain.
items.cn: 现代英语中 buy 扩展到相信与划算的买卖。

items.en: The noun buy names a purchase or a bargain.
items.cn: 名词 buy 指一次购买或划算货。

definition_en: the country in North America
core_image: 一片北方的土地上，枫叶落在雪边，湖泊一望无际
scene: 地图上北边那片土地，枫叶标志贴在最上面。Her cousin lives in Canada.
sceneCN: 这里 canada 是「加拿大」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她的表亲住在加拿大。

derivatives.zh: 由 Canada 加 -ian 构成，义为「加拿大的」
由 Canada 加 -iana 构成，义为「加拿大文物」
由 Canada 与 Day 复合，义为「加拿大国庆日」

senses.title: The country in the north of North America
senses.definition: the country occupying the northern part of North America
senses.definitionCN: 占据北美洲北部的国家
senses.example: Her cousin lives in Canada.
senses.exampleCN: 她的表亲住在加拿大。
senses.why: Canada comes from kanata, a word in the language of the St Lawrence peoples meaning 'village'; French explorers took it for the name of the whole land.
senses.whyCN: Canada 来自圣劳伦斯河一带原住民语中的 kanata「村落」，法国探险家误把它当作整片土地的名字。

senses.title: Used in names of plants and animals of that region
senses.titleCN: 加拿大的（用于动植物名）
senses.definition: placed before the name of a species associated with Canada, as in Canada goose
senses.definitionCN: 放在物种名前，表示与加拿大有关，如 Canada goose
senses.example: A Canada goose landed on the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 一只加拿大雁落在池塘上。
senses.why: Some species are so closely tied to that country that its name became part of their everyday name, as with the Canada goose.
senses.whyCN: 有些物种与这个国家关系密切，国名就成了它们日常名称的一部分，比如加拿大雁。

items.en: The name spread across the British colonies.

items.en: Canada became the country's name in 1867.

definition_en: a sweet food made with sugar, or to cook fruit in sugar
core_image: 玻璃罐里装着一颗颗彩色糖块，罐壁被光打得发亮
scene: 玻璃罐里装着一把彩色糖块，孩子们踮脚去够。The children were given candy after lunch.
sceneCN: 这里 candy 是「糖果」（第 01 个义项）；句意是午饭后孩子们得到了糖果。

derivatives.zh: 由 candy 加 -ed 构成，义为「糖渍的」
由 candy 与 maker 复合，义为「糖果制造商」
由 candy 与 floss 复合，义为「棉花糖」

senses.title: Sweet food made with sugar
senses.definition: a sweet food made mainly of sugar, often eaten as a treat
senses.definitionCN: 主要用糖做成、当零食吃的甜食
senses.example: The children were given candy after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭后孩子们得到了糖果。
senses.why: Candy came from Old French sucre candi, 'candied sugar', which traces back through Arabic qandī to Sanskrit, and it now covers sugar sweets generally.
senses.whyCN: candy 来自古法语 sucre candi「糖渍的糖」，经阿拉伯语 qandī 上溯至梵语，如今泛指糖做的甜食。

senses.title: To preserve fruit in sugar
senses.definition: to cook or preserve fruit in sugar
senses.definitionCN: 把水果用糖煮或腌起来
senses.example: She candied the orange peel for the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她把橙皮糖渍了做蛋糕。
senses.why: The noun gave a verb: to candy something is to treat it with sugar until it keeps and sweetens.
senses.whyCN: 名词生出动词：candy 某物就是用糖处理它，让它耐放又甜。

intro.en: The history of candy is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: candy 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Candi meant crystallised sugar.
items.cn: 法语 candi 指结晶的糖。

items.en: The French word came from Arabic qandi.
items.cn: 这个法语词来自阿拉伯语 qandi。

items.en: Persian qand meant sugar.
items.cn: 波斯语 qand 意为糖。

items.en: English shortened candi to candy.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪把 candi 缩短为 candy。

items.en: Candy covers sweets, colours and the verb to candy fruit.
items.cn: 现代英语中 candy 覆盖糖果、颜色与糖渍动词。

definition_zh: 帽子；盖；帽状物；覆盖；上限
definition_en: a soft hat with a peak, a lid, or an upper limit
core_image: 一顶带檐的布帽扣在头上，帽檐压住眉线
scene: 门口的人把帽檐压低，挡住斜射进来的光。He wore a blue cap to the game.
sceneCN: 这里 cap 是「帽子」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他戴着一顶蓝帽去看比赛。

derivatives.zh: 由 cap 加 -ed 构成，义为「有上限的」
由 cap 加 -ful 构成，义为「一帽之量」
由 cap 与 stone 复合，义为「顶石」

senses.title: A soft hat with a peak
senses.definition: a soft hat with a flat peak, worn on the head
senses.definitionCN: 有帽檐、戴在头上的软帽
senses.example: He wore a blue cap to the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一顶蓝帽去看比赛。
senses.why: Cap came through Latin cappa, 'head covering', and Old English cæppe, and the head-covering sense is its base.
senses.whyCN: cap 经拉丁语 cappa「头巾」和古英语 cæppe 而来，盖在头上的东西是它的本义。

senses.title: A lid or top for a container
senses.definition: a lid or covering for the top of a bottle or tube
senses.definitionCN: 瓶口或管口上的盖
senses.example: The bottle cap rolled under the table.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶盖滚到了桌子底下。
senses.why: A cap covers the head; a lid covers the top of a bottle, so the same word serves both coverings.
senses.whyCN: 帽子盖着头，瓶盖盖着瓶口，同一种「盖」的用法就用同一个词。

senses.title: An upper limit
senses.definition: a fixed upper limit on an amount or a price
senses.definitionCN: 数量或价格上封顶的界限
senses.example: The government set a cap on fuel prices.
senses.exampleCN: 政府给燃料价格设了上限。
senses.why: A cap seals the top so nothing can rise higher, and that picture became a limit on numbers.
senses.whyCN: 盖子封住顶端，东西再也不能往上冒，这个画面就变成了数字上的上限。

senses.title: To cover the top of something
senses.definition: to cover the top of something, as snow covers a hill
senses.definitionCN: 像雪盖住山顶那样盖在某物的顶部
senses.example: Snow capped the hills before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前雪盖住了山冈。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so to cap a hill is to put a cap of snow or ice on it.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，cap 一座山就是给它盖上一层雪或冰。

senses.title: To set an upper limit on something
senses.definition: to put a fixed upper limit on an amount or price
senses.definitionCN: 给数量或价格封顶
senses.example: The city capped the bus fare at two dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 市里把公交车费封顶在两美元。
senses.why: The limiting sense of the noun also became a verb: to cap a fare is to put a lid on how high it can go.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「上限」义也转成动词：cap a fare 就是给票价盖上一个盖子，不许再涨。

intro.en: The history of cap is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: cap 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Cappa meant a hood or head covering.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cappa 指头巾或罩帽。

items.en: Cæppe came from Latin and meant a cap or hood.
items.cn: 古英语 cæppe 来自拉丁语，指帽子或头巾。

items.en: Cap named hats and covers.
items.cn: 中古英语中 cap 指帽子与盖子。

items.en: The upper-limit sense grew in modern English.
items.cn: 上限义在现代英语中发展出来。

items.en: The national-team sense comes from the cap given to players.
items.cn: 国家队义来自发给球员的帽子。
